title: Digital cardiovascular prevention
summary:
High blood pressure, physical inactivity, smoking, and other risk factors are major causes of numerous serious illnesses such as heart attack, heart failure, and stroke. However, current scientific studies show that up to 80% of all cardiovascular diseases could be prevented with preventative measures.

Within the framework of the EFRE-funded research project "Digital Cardiovascular Prevention – DICAP," our interdisciplinary project team is investigating the potential of telemedicine-based prevention.

interventions.name: Telemedical monitoring of blood pressure, body weight, ECG, and physical activity. Digital educational modules on cardiovascular prevention. Telemedical optimization of cardiovascular risk factors (12 months, measurement at baseline and end of study)
Care as usual therapy of risk factors (12 months, measurement at baseline and end of study)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Arterial hypertension + one other cardiovascular risk factor (physical inactivity, obesity, hypercholesterolemia, smoking, diabetes mellitus)
-MRI suitability (no tinnitus, no tattoos, no magnetic implants)
Exclusion criteria:
1. A history of a cardiovascular or neurovascular event (heart attack, stroke)
2. Relevant and uncontrolled supraventricular or ventricular arrhythmias (except adequately rate-controlled atrial fibrillation)
3. (Moderate) and/or intervention-requiring valvular heart disease or symptomatic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF)
4. A history of substantial neurological or psychiatric disorders (e.g., seizure disorder, severe traumatic brain injury, depression, schizophrenia, dementia)
5. An implanted pacemaker
6. Malignant diseases with a reduced life expectancy
